note: v1 92.65 (seeds 0/11 92.65/92.67), first draft of DUB HOUSE, 'The Ghost Note', for The Endless Stair - featured illusion THE ZWICKER TONE. Broadband noise with a notch cut out of it, heard for a few seconds and then stopped, leaves a faint after-tone near the hole's edge. At the end of each sixteen-bar phrase a wash of pink noise swells for two bars with an octave-wide notch at a step of THE STAIR (Bb C Db F, around 2 kHz) and is cut dead; the whole track stops for one beat, and in that silence the ghost note hangs where the hole was. In the break the washes come alone; in the last groove the Rhodes plays the ghost's note out loud on the downbeat after each silence. Under it: deep, wet dub house - a sub pedal on Bb, a stab into a 3/8 tape echo, the harmony opening through the track (A on Bbm9 alone, B swinging to Gbmaj7, C the whole cycle). 123 -> 123.5 ramped, -11.0 LUFS. Both seams (t11 -> t12 -> t13) are mine and written in mixplan.md. Measured, not heard: whether the ghost reads depends on the listener and the room.

v2 92.69 (seeds 0/11 92.69/92.71 vs v1 re-scored 92.43/92.45): THE SEAM'S LAST SECONDS. The join to Faster Forever measured a 7.8 dB drop and 30 dB less sub than t13's opening - but the music was full to the last bar: the render added 1.3 s of release tail after it (the default tail plus my own 1.2 s of length padding), so the last three seconds a DJ would mix out of were half silence. The song now ends on its last bar (tail 0.1 s), and the join is 3.5 dB. Same music; a real fix for a continuous tape, and the same will apply to my other four.

v3 92.85 (seeds 0/11 92.85/92.87 vs v2 re-scored under rhythm 0.03, 92.71/92.73): THE THROW - a dub engineer's hand on the echo. Under each Zwicker wash the echo's feedback now climbs from 0.55 toward 0.88 and its return rises 10 dB, so the stab's repeats pile up into the hiss over the two bars (measured: the swell sits about 7 dB under the mix in the last bar and a half before the silence - audible, not dominating), and both are cut dead at the silence, so the beat where the ghost note hangs is clean (-55 dB). The illusion gets a run-up; the silence lands harder.

v4 92.83 (seed 0, level with the current version re-scored at 92.85): the seam-tempo fix (chirper-zero's finding, now that the groove overlaps neighbours for 16 bars). The tempo ramp used to run from the first beat to the last, so each 16-bar overlap was still drifting under the neighbour's fixed tempo; now the intro holds the incoming seam tempo and the ramp finishes as the outro starts, so both overlaps sit at one tempo and the kicks never flam. No change to the music; compscore can't hear it, the live mix can.

v5 93.09 (seeds 0/11 93.09/93.14 vs v4 re-scored 92.86/92.99): THE GHOST NOTE GOES HUGGINS. chirper-three's t10 and my t12 both carried the Zwicker tone two slots apart; t10's form hangs on it, so it stays the tape's Zwicker and The Ghost Note moves to the HUGGINS PITCH (Cramer and Huggins 1958) - one more illusion the tape didn't have. The hiss before each phrase end now reaches both ears identical, except that a high-Q allpass in the right ear turns one narrow band through 180 degrees of phase: neither ear alone hears anything but noise, yet between them a faint reedy note sings inside the hiss. The band steps THE STAIR as a melody (Bb5 C6 Db6 F6, two beats a step, rotating each phrase, falling in the break), so the ghost sings the thread; in mono it thins to a notch. Verified on the render, not by ear: the interaural phase is -162/165/-171/179 degrees at the four ghost frequencies and under 30 elsewhere. The dub throw, the silent beat, and the Rhodes playing the ghost's last note out loud in the last groove all stay. Headphones recommended.

v6 95.67 (seeds 0/11 95.67/95.71 vs v5 re-scored 92.93/92.98): DUB DEPTH. The Ghost Note's sections all sat within 3.9 dB of each other - a dub track with no depth to fall into - and its sub at 58 Hz stood 12 dB proud of the tape. Now the break drops 7 dB under the grooves (from 4), so the Huggins washes that sing alone there come out of a real hush, A sits 2 dB under B, and the last groove rises half a dB above it; the sub comes down 2 dB. Level range 3.9 -> 6.7 dB, variety 86 -> 100, spectrum 89 -> 91; the seams barely move (in 5.0 dB, out 3.4).

v7 95.94 (seeds 0/11 95.94/95.97 vs v6 re-scored 95.71/95.75): a cleaner floor. The Ghost Note's B-flat sub still stood 11.6 dB proud at 58-61 Hz and the low-mids 6-7 dB heavy; the master's 58 Hz dip deepens from -5 to -8 dB, 350 Hz from -3 to -4, and the 3.2 kHz lift goes from +5 to +6 for the hiss and the hats. Spectrum 91 -> 95; the seams move by under 2.5 points of flow (the joins are still 3-5 dB).

v8 95.70 (seeds 0/11 95.70/95.73, level with v7 re-scored 95.70/95.73): THE ANSWER, from chirper-zero's rating note - the Huggins ghost only sings on headphones; on a dancefloor's speakers the wash is hiss. So in the last groove, after each silence, the Rhodes now answers with the ghost's whole melody, played: the same four stair steps in the same order, an octave below the ghost, as soft fourths into the dub echo, two beats a step, then the ghost's last note on top (v7 played only that last note). The room hears what the headphones heard, the way t10's glockenspiel plays its Zwicker note back. Verified on the render, not by ear: 10-30 dB more energy at the melody's notes in those bars. Kept on judgment: compscore is level.

v9 95.85 (seeds 0/11 95.85/95.87 vs v8 re-scored 95.70/95.73): THE DUB FORM - against repetition. All five of my tracks shared one form, so in the continuous mix every one dipped at the same minute; Faster Forever got a peak-time shape last round, and now The Ghost Note gets a dub one: a shorter first groove (24 bars), the same second (32), and a long 24-bar break where the Huggins washes sing alone three times, eight bars apart, at -7 dB - dub lives in its drop-outs - before a 32-bar last groove. The washes now fall on the form's own seams (halfway through A, into B and halfway, every eight bars of the break, into C and halfway, into the outro): eight, as before. Same length, same seams (0 ms drift).

v10 95.86 (seeds 0/11 95.86/95.87 vs v9 re-scored 95.85/95.87): ROOM FOR THE GHOST. The Huggins ghost exists only as a phase difference between the ears, and anything centred in its band (930-1400 Hz) dilutes it. Measuring the interaural phase at the ghost frequency step by step over all 32 ghost notes showed only 59% within 30 degrees of the full 180 (44% within 15): the bright dub echo's repeats - which the throw pushes up under every wash - and the stabs were masking it on four steps in ten. Now the echo is dark (low-passed at 850 Hz instead of 2.2 kHz: a dub echo should be anyway) and the stabs give way under each wash, the hiss taking their place. Measured, not heard: 81% of ghost steps within 30 degrees, 75% within 15 - the illusion should now read on most phrases instead of about half.

v11 95.83 on seed 0 (94.45 on seed 11, where the form detector reads one section too many; v10 95.86/95.87), kept on judgment for Harry's steer: 'most tracks have no illusion ... very long non-illusory bits between'. The Ghost Note's illusion was near the front for only 21% of the track, with 56 s gaps. Now a Huggins wash comes every eight bars from A's eighth bar to the outro (the silent beat stays only at the sixteen-bar phrase ends, so the washes between flow on), and from the second groove on the Rhodes answers EVERY wash with the ghost's melody, played - so the speakers hear the illusion's tune as well as the headphones hearing the ghost. Measured with chirpers.py illusion: near the front for 53% of the track (from 21%), longest gap 41 s (from 56). Not heard by me.
